title: Seven fat cows
hookLine: the cupbearer finally remembers, and Yusuf reads the king's dream as seven good years and seven hard
carry: the fat years feed the thin

cards: Years pass. Yusuf is still in prison, forgotten by the man who promised to mention him. Then the king of Egypt has a dream that won't leave him alone.
He tells his court: I saw seven fat cows, and seven lean cows eating them. And seven green ears of grain, and seven others, dry. Tell me what it means.
His advisers have no answer. Jumbled dreams, they say, and we don't know how to read those. And the freed prisoner, the one who pours the king's wine, hears it all.
The Qur'an says he remembered, after a long time. Send me, he says. I know someone.

teach.b: Surah Yusuf. The cupbearer comes to the cell and says: Yusuf, you truthful one, explain this dream to us. Truthful one.
Years later, he still remembers the thing that mattered about Yusuf. Now watch what Yusuf does. He doesn't say, first get me out of here.
He doesn't say, you forgot me.
He doesn't bargain at all. He answers, and goes further than he was asked. For seven years, he says, farm as you usually do.
What you harvest, leave in the ear, on the stalk, except the little you eat. Then seven hard years will come that eat up what you stored, except a little you keep back.
Then a year will come when people have rain, and they'll press fruit and oil again. The king asked for a meaning.
Yusuf gives him a plan: save in the good years, store the grain in the ear, where it keeps, eat a little, not a lot. And he adds a year the dream never mentioned, a fifteenth year of relief.

That's a hopeful reader of dreams: he sees past the famine to the rain. Jews and Christians tell this story too, in Genesis, where Joseph reads Pharaoh's dream in much the same way. Good seasons don't last.

teach.h: THE FAT YEARS FEED THE THIN.
teach.b: The wise thing is to let the fat years feed the thin. And Yusuf, still in his cell, has just given Egypt a way through the hard years without asking for a thing.

how: Muslims draw practical wisdom from Yusuf's interpretation, saving and planning in times of plenty, and often cite it in teaching about stewardship and preparing for hardship.

games.q: you're Yusuf, forgotten in prison for years. the man who forgot you comes to ask about the king's dream. what do you do?
o: say: get me out first, then I'll tell you.
give the meaning, and a plan for the hard years.
games.why: no bargain, no blame. he gives a plan: farm seven years, store in the ear, eat a little, and after the hard years, a year of rain.

practice: Think about what you have plenty of right now, money this week, or energy, time, patience, a friend's goodwill; whatever season you're in, something is usually fat.
Picture putting one small portion by, in the ear: five dollars into savings, a meal into the freezer, an hour of rest before the busy week, a kind message to someone before you need them.
If you pray, you can give thanks for the plenty.
